findings.title: Blob URL for backup-codes download is never revoked on close or unmount
findings.body: When the setup step succeeds, a Blob URL is created from the backup codes and stored in `backupCodesUrl`. `URL.revokeObjectURL` is only called when a fresh URL is generated, so when the user closes the modal (which calls `resetState`, which doesn't touch `backupCodesUrl`) or the component unmounts, the previous Blob and its URL remain pinned in memory until the page reloads. This is a slow leak that accumulates each time a user opens the enable flow, and it also leaves a stale `blob:` URL reachable from the previous render. Add a useEffect cleanup (or revoke in `resetState` and on `onOpenChange(false)`) so the URL is released whenever the modal closes or the component unmounts.

findings.title: TOCTOU race allows a single backup code to be used to log in more than once
findings.body: The backup-code branch decrypts `user.backupCodes`, calls `indexOf`, sets `backupCodes[index] = null`, then re-encrypts and `prisma.user.update`s — but this is done as separate read/transform/write with no `WHERE backupCodes = ...` predicate or transaction. Two concurrent login attempts using the same code both find it at the same index before either write lands, both set the slot to null, and both succeed. Backup codes are explicitly documented as single-use, so reuse defeats the feature. Either wrap the read+write in a transaction with a predicate that matches the current `backupCodes` value (optimistic concurrency) or, better, persist codes as rows so consumption can be a single atomic UPDATE/DELETE on the matching row.

findings.title: Uncaught JSON.parse on decrypted backupCodes can crash every login for affected user
findings.body: `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY))` will throw if the stored ciphertext is ever tampered with, truncated, or encrypted under a different `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` (e.g. a key rotation on a self-hosted deployment). The throw is not caught, so the NextAuth `authorize` call aborts with a generic exception and the user — including admins — is locked out of their own account with no actionable error. Wrap the decrypt+parse in try/catch and return `ErrorCode.InternalServerError` (or a clearer code) so the response is well-formed and the failure is logged with the user id, instead of an unhandled exception surfacing through NextAuth.

findings.title: Uncaught JSON.parse on decrypted backupCodes can break 2FA disable
findings.body: Same issue as in `next-auth-options.ts`: `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY))` is not wrapped in try/catch. If the encrypted payload is unreadable (corruption, schema drift after key rotation, partial DB write), the handler throws an uncaught error and the user is unable to disable 2FA via a backup code — which is the very path designed for 'lost access'. The handler should catch the failure, log it, and return a clear error (e.g. `ErrorCode.MissingBackupCodes` or `InternalServerError`) rather than letting it bubble to a 500.

findings.title: Backup code comparison is case-sensitive though generated codes are lowercase hex
findings.body: `crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` always emits lowercase, but the lookup uses `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` with no `.toLowerCase()` and no `.trim()`. A user who pastes or types a code with caps, surrounding whitespace, or different separators (space, period) will get `IncorrectBackupCode` even though they have a valid code, which is especially painful here because the input is a long hex string with no character-class hint. Normalize the input (`replaceAll("-", "").replace(/\s+/g, "").toLowerCase()`) on both the login and the `disable` handler so users don't silently burn codes for a casing/whitespace mismatch.

findings.title: No end-to-end coverage for backup code login or backup-code disable flow
findings.body: The PR adds the new backup-code login branch in `next-auth-options.ts`, the new `backupCode` field in the login form, and a new disable-via-backup-code branch in `disable.ts` and `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`. The e2e file only exercises the post-enable display dialog (download/copy/close buttons) and does not cover the security-critical paths: logging in with a backup code, exercising the 'Lost access' toggle on the login page, or disabling 2FA via a backup code (the exact flow the feature was built for, and which is gated by `twoFactorLostAccess` and `backupCode` in `DisableTwoFactorModal`). The author explicitly flagged this as a TODO at line 12. Given that backup-code handling involves the TOCTOU race and decrypt-and-parse logic reviewed in the other findings, an e2e that signs in with a valid code and a second time with the same code (expecting rejection) is necessary before merging.
